newsitem.title: JAPAN: Reform delays may shift business out of Japan-BOJ.
newsitem.headline: Reform delays may shift business out of Japan-BOJ.

text.p: Bank of Japan (BOJ) governor Yasuo Matsushita said on Friday that there is a possibility that financial transactions will be shifted overseas if Japan fails to carry out various deregulations on schedule.

"If financial deregulation other than the foreign exchange laws is delayed, we cannot deny the possibility that financial transactions in Japanese markets will shift overseas," Matsushita told a key budget committee of the Lower House of parliament.
The governor said the basic idea behind Japan's "Big Bang" financial reforms to create free and active Tokyo markets was timely and appropriate.
Matsushita said he strongly hoped that detailed plans would be drawn up soon for the actual implementation of the deregulation steps.
Moves to deregulate the foreign exchange law are important steps towards a review of all financial markets, he added.
